correctness.rationale: For i!=j the closed-neighborhood symmetric difference N[a_i] Δ N[a_j] equals P_i ∪ P_j, forcing at most one empty matched pair; hence |C|>=n-1. Equality forces one hole and one code endpoint from each remaining pair. For A-side traces, selected a_i gives {a_i}∪B_Q, unselected a_i gives B_Q\{b_i}, and the hole gives B_Q; symmetric B traces. If either chosen-side count is <2 a zero trace or collision results; for >=2 on each side all 2n traces are nonempty, same-side distinct and cross-side disjoint except impossible singleton cases. Count choose hole n times and orient n-1 occupied indices excluding side counts 0,1,n-2,n-1: n(2^(n-1)-2n). Reconstructed definitions and all n>=5 boundary. Independently enumerated all size n−1 subsets for n=5,6,7,8 with totals 30,120,350,896; finite enumeration corroborates but does not prove all n.

value.rationale: The standard extremal crown family has a known scalar identifying-code minimum, but its ENTIRE optimizer set and exact count are natural additional invariants for classification/symmetry and code-selection questions. The two-per-side obstruction and exceptional n=5 onset distinguish it from the easy lower bound. This is a self-contained all-n structural classification, not a mere known-number recomputation.

final_claim: For n>=5 the balanced crown Cr_n=K_{n,n} minus its perfect matching has identifying-code minimum n-1 (already prior art); every minimum code omits exactly one matched index and selects exactly one endpoint of every other pair with at least two selections per side; the number of minima is n(2^(n-1)-2n).
limitations: Restricted to n>=5 and closed-neighborhood identifying codes.
No novelty claim for scalar γ_ID(Cr_n)=n−1.
